decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoNoSpacing">The
proposal, by reason of failing to provide private rear amenity space for the FF
flat, would result in a poor standard of living accommodation for future
occupiers of this unit, to the detriment of their residential amenities,&nbsp; contrary to the National Planning Policy
Framework (2023), Policies D6 and D3, of the London Plan (2021), Policies DM 1
and DM 26 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013),
The&nbsp; Mayor of London Housing
Supplementary Planning Guidance (2016), the adopted Supplementary Planning
Document: Residential Design Guide (2010) and Housing Design Standards LPG
(2023).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoNoSpacing">The
proposed height and proximity of the proposed rear and side infill extension would create a sense of enclosure to neighbouring windows and reduce outlook causing detrimental loss of neighbouring residential amenity. As such, this would harm to the amenities of neighbouring
residential units contrary to the high design aspirations of the National
Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021), Core
Policy CS1 (B) of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), policy DM 1 of the Harrow
Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the adopted Supplementary
Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoNoSpacing">The proposal, by reason of the insufficient number of
cycle storage provided within the garage/car port space and the seemingly
inaccessibility of this space to the first-floor flat, would result in the
unsatisfactory provision of safe cycle storage facilities, to provide
facilities for all the users of the site and in the interests of highway safety
and sustainable transport, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), &nbsp;Policy T5 of The London Plan (2021) and Policy
DM 42 of the Harrow Development Management Policies (2013).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoNoSpacing">The proposed rear dormer by reason of its considerable
width and massing along the rear roof space of the property as well as the
proposed dormer wrapping around the roof over the two-storey rear outrigger would
add significant additional bulk and massing, resulting in a top heavy addition dominating the rear roof slope and visually prominent in the streetsene. As such, the dormer design is contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National
Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D3.D(1) and D3.D(11) of the London
Plan (2021), Policy CS.1B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the
Development Management Plan Local Policies (2013) and the Adopted Supplementary
Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoNoSpacing">The
proposal, by reason of failing to provide minimum bedroom areas for the future
residents of the bedrooms in the GF Flat, as well as poor lighting, outlook and
a lack of defensible space to the ground floor single bedroom and poor lighting
to the first-floor bedroom, would result in a poor standard of living
accommodation for future occupiers of those flats, to the detriment of their
residential amenities,&nbsp; contrary to the
National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D6 and D3, of the London
Plan (2021), Policies DM 1 and DM 26 of the Harrow Development Management
Policies Local Plan (2013), The&nbsp; Mayor of
London Housing Supplementary Planning Guidance (2016), the adopted
Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010) and Housing
Design Standards LPG (2023).<o:p></o:p></p>
description: Conversion of dwelling into two flats (2 X 2 bed); single storey side to rear extension; alterations to roof; rear dormer with Juliette balcony; two rooflights in front roofslope; extension to detached garage at rear for use as cycle storage; rear amenity space for Flat 1; parking; bin store to front; external alterations (demolition of rear extension)
